name: Seam-Gap Backtest
question: When pitchers with the same spin get more movement, does the flagged pitch move toward them the next season?
data: Season N = 2025, N+1 = 2026. Flags use only data through 2025: spin twins from 2021-2025 and Stuff+ trained on 2021-2024. 2026 outcomes are not used until this test runs, once.
method: Season N is 2025 and N+1 is 2026. The flags use only data through 2025: spin twins from 2021–2025 and Stuff+ trained on 2021–2024.

A pitch is flagged the way Grip Candidates are: 8+ tight spin twins, 3+ of them (and a third) with better run value, a movement gap of 1.5 inches to 3 times the twins' own spread, and 60%+ efficiency.
For flagged pitches thrown 100+ times in 2026 whose movement changed by 2+ inches, the test asks whether the 2026 movement landed inside the 80% region where the 2025 twins' movement sits.
Each result has a 95% range from resampling pitchers 2,000 times. The decision uses the measured share.

registered_metrics.description: Changed flagged pitches landing inside the twins' 80% movement region
registered_metrics.sample: Flagged pitches thrown 100+ times in 2026 whose movement changed by 2+ inches (IVB and HB distance).
registered_metrics.statistic: Share whose 2026 movement falls inside the 80% highest-density region of their 2025 tight twins' movement (weighted 2D kernel density, the same method as Potential envelopes).

gate_rule: Passes if coverage is between 0.70 and 0.90 (the region is calibrated). Decisions use the point estimate.
uncertainty: 95% intervals by bootstrap over pitchers (2,000 resamples, seed 11), reported alongside, not used to decide.

results.note: 33 of 127 flagged pitches changed movement by 2+ inches.
results.value_label: Share of changed flagged pitches inside the twins' region

reported.description: Share of flagged pitches that changed movement by 2+ inches (vs. unflagged pitches)
Among changed flagged pitches, share that moved toward the better twins' movement (positive projection on the gap)
Stuff+ change of changed flagged pitches minus changed unflagged pitches
The spec's original flag (Stuff+ main lever is seam, seam percentile 25 or lower): the same statistics
reported.note: Changed share 96/322; toward the best point 0.66; inside the 80% envelope 0.43; Stuff+ change +0.3.

conclusion: Failed. When flagged pitches changed shape (33 of 127), 58% of them landed inside the region their 2025 spin twins occupy; the registered line was 70–90%. So the twins' region is too narrow to say where a changed pitch will land. Reported only: they moved toward the better twins 64% of the time (50% is a coin flip) and gained 2.4 more Stuff+ than other pitches that changed, on a small sample. The line stays as registered.
badge: Backtest T2 (2025 to 2026) failed: when flagged pitches changed, 58% landed inside their spin twins' region (pass line 70–90%). They did move toward the better twins 64% of the time and gained 2.4 more Stuff+ than other changed pitches (33 pitches, a small sample).
limitations: One season pair (2025 to 2026) and few flagged pitches that changed (see the samples), so the ranges are wide.
A pitch that changed movement may have changed spin too (speed, efficiency, direction), not only seams; this test doesn't separate them.
Run value per 100 pitches, used to call a twin "better," is noisy for one season.
The region is drawn from the twins' season averages, which vary less than a single pitcher's year-to-year changes.

charts.title: Flagged Pitches That Changed: Movement Toward Twins vs. Stuff+ Change
charts.summary: 33 flagged pitches whose movement changed by 2+ inches. Right of zero: moved toward the twins with better results.
